Changes.Change: Rewritten for this engine; rooms in different states merged into single scenes
Fights and tests re-tuned and scaled: DEATH & TREASURE is not used
Enemy morale not implemented; the chance of a random encounter is ours
Abilities renamed, and tests the original left open assigned by us
Original illustrations not included: they are not licensed with the text
A pilot: it covers the entrance and one room, and stops there

Skill.name: Toughness
Skill.description: How much poison, gas and exhaustion you can take.

Skill.name: Agility
Skill.description: Squeezing through tight places, slipping past what is watching.

Skill.name: Strength
Skill.description: Shifting stone, forcing what will not move.

Skill.name: Instinct
Skill.description: Noticing what is out of place, reading a room before it reads you.

Page.Title: The stair of weathered jade
Page.Text:
VIPERBLOOD, an emerald green water rumoured to be found only in the First Crypt, is said to cure anything that afflicts humankind. The king is deathly ill. One at a time he is sending out "volunteers" from his court to retrieve some for him. It is your turn now. Any treasure you find is yours to keep as a reward for your service.
You have been equipped with a magic scroll on which you can write notes about what you find and record a map of the crypt. It returns to the castle upon the death of its bearer. It already carries a map, and the notes left by previous "volunteers".
Guards escort you to the ancient burial grounds. In the back, far from the paths maintained for mourners of the recent dead, is the crypt of the ancient queens: the First Crypt. They leave you in front of a stair, roughly hewn into weathered jade stone, which passes steeply up to a massive facade, an entryway, and statues looming over you. Cold air wafts slowly down the steps to your feet.

Choice.text: Climb the steps and enter the crypt

Page.Title: The hall of the jade serpent
Page.Text:
You stand at the entrance on the east side of a large hall, lit faintly by the light from the opening behind you. The space is full, wall to wall and floor to ceiling, with an enormous jade statue of a snake, twisting and turning over itself, tying itself in knots, but with space enough to move through them.
The head of the snake is to your right, mouth open, large pointed fangs ready to strike. Behind the fangs it appears there is a tunnel inside the snake.
At your feet is a skein of pure white yarn, glowing with a slightly magical aura.

Text.Content: A white thread runs away from your feet and disappears among the coils. You laid it yourself, and it still marks the way through.

Choice.text: Climb into the mouth and follow the tunnel inside the snake
Work around the coils, unspooling the yarn behind you
Work around the coils with nothing but your hands
Follow the white thread to the far corner

Page.Title: Inside the serpent
Page.Text: You push through the cramped tunnel and find that inside it is far less complicated than it appears from without. Rather than twists and turns it takes you on a relatively straight path north, opening up into a new chamber.

Page.Title: The thread holds
Page.Text: You work your way carefully over, under and around the intertwining body of the stone snake. It is slow work, and the yarn magically strings itself out as you go, marking a quick path through the statue. You will not have to guess again.

Choice.text: Come out in the far corner of the hall

Page.Title: Back where you started
Page.Text: Try as you might, you cannot make heads or tails of how to go through this snake. The coils bring you round on yourself, and you eventually find yourself back where you started, out of breath and no wiser.

Choice.text: Stand again at the eastern entrance
Stand again in the far corner

Page.Title: Over, under, around
Page.Text: You work your way carefully over, under and around the intertwining body of the stone snake. It is slow work, and you do not recall your exact path: you will have to spend the same time again the next time you cross this room.

Choice.text: Come out in the far corner of the hall

Page.Title: The far corner
Page.Text: In the south-west corner of the hall are two sets of double doors: one on the south wall, one on the west wall. Behind you the jade coils stand between you and the daylight of the entrance.

Text.Content: Your white thread comes out of the coils here, and runs back the way you came.

Choice.text: Push open the double doors on the south wall
Cross back towards the entrance, working around the coils
Follow the white thread back to the entrance

Page.Title: You can go on
Page.Text: When it is over you stand still for a while, listening to the hall. Nothing else moves among the coils. You pick up where you left off and finish crossing.

Choice.text: Come out in the far corner of the hall

Page.Title: You died
Page.Text: You died in the hall of the jade serpent. The magic scroll returns to the castle on its own, carrying your notes and your map. Future adventurers may find your body, and take anything you were carrying.

Choice.text: Take a new volunteer from the court and begin again

Page.Title: Here the pilot ends
Page.Text:
Beyond this door the crypt goes on: a dark room with bronze sconces, a grotto where a stone faun pours dark water, a room strung wall to wall with tripwires, and much further in, the emerald water the king is dying for.
This conversion stops here. What you have played is the entrance and the hall of the jade serpent, converted from Luke Simonds's Viperblood to find out whether it fits the engine.

Page.Title: Four rabets, and a dead snake
Page.Text: Four rabets come round the coils dragging a dead snake by the tail. They stop when they see you. The one at the front lets go of the tail, and the body slaps against the jade.

Enemy.name: Four rabets dragging a dead snake

Page.Title: Hunting
Page.Text: You hear them before you see them: five snakes moving fast and low over the stone, spread out the way things spread out when they are hunting together.

Enemy.name: A pack of five hunting snakes

Page.Title: Two rabets, lost
Page.Text: Two rabets come round a coil arguing in low barks, and stop dead. They are not where they meant to be, and neither of them expected you.

Enemy.name: Two lost rabets

Page.Title: A snake taking a nap
Page.Text: A snake lies coiled in a hollow of the statue, out of the draught, asleep. You could try to get past it. It might not stay asleep.

Enemy.name: A snake woken badly

Page.Title: Two parties at once
Page.Text: Four rabets come round the coils with a dead snake, and behind them, drawn by the noise, four more. Nobody backs off.

Enemy.name: Four rabets dragging a dead snake
Four more rabets, drawn by the noise

Page.Title: Hunters and hunted, both here
Page.Text: Four rabets are dragging their dead snake past you when the pack that has been following the smell arrives. For a moment nobody is sure who is fighting whom. The moment passes.

Enemy.name: Four rabets dragging a dead snake
A pack of five hunting snakes

Page.Title: The party and the strays
Page.Text: Four rabets with a dead snake, and two more who have clearly been looking for them. Finding you first does not improve anybody's temper.

Enemy.name: Four rabets dragging a dead snake
Two lost rabets

Page.Title: Enough noise to wake it
Page.Text: Four rabets come round the coils dragging a dead snake. They are not quiet about it, and in the hollow above you something that was asleep stops being asleep.

Enemy.name: Four rabets dragging a dead snake
A snake woken badly

Page.Title: Two packs, one corridor of stone
Page.Text: Snakes come from both sides of the coil at once. They are not hunting each other, which leaves only you.

Enemy.name: A pack of five hunting snakes
A second pack, coming the other way

Page.Title: The strays run into the pack
Page.Text: Two lost rabets come round the coil at a trot, see you, and stop. Behind them the hunting pack that has been herding them all along arrives.

Enemy.name: A pack of five hunting snakes
Two lost rabets

Page.Title: The pack, and what it wakes
Page.Text: The hunting pack pours over the jade, and the noise brings the sleeper out of its hollow behind you.

Enemy.name: A pack of five hunting snakes
A snake woken badly

Page.Title: Four rabets, none of whom know the way
Page.Text: Two rabets come round the coil, and two more from the other side, all of them lost, all of them relieved to see somebody until they see it is you.

Enemy.name: Two lost rabets
Two more lost rabets

Page.Title: They step on it before you do
Page.Text: Two lost rabets come round the coil at a bad angle and one of them puts a foot in the hollow where the snake is sleeping. Now none of you have a choice.

Enemy.name: Two lost rabets
A snake woken badly

Page.Title: Two hollows, two sleepers
Page.Text: There is a snake asleep in the hollow ahead of you and another in the hollow behind, and the stone carries every sound you make to both of them.

Enemy.name: A snake woken badly
A second snake, woken worse
